label: TP
reason: User-supplied HTTP header names flow directly into the HTML response via ESAPI.encodeForHTML(new String(input)). Although the header NAME itself is used as the variable name in the Java code (param), the actual content written to the browser comes from the decrypted bytes derived from the HEADER VALUE (which contains the original header name). Since header names are user-controllable and the encoder is applied to the final output string containing the header name, an attacker can inject arbitrary characters (like <script>) into the header name, which then appears unescaped in the HTML response.

evidence.note: Header names extracted from request populate param, passed to doSomething, then converted to bytes and encoded for HTML output; header names are user-controllable and reach the sink
